title: Checkpointed streaming + page adapter for embeddings/rerank compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a compatibility layer that exposes a hybrid streaming + pagination semantics for embeddings and rerank endpoints. Legacy vector-search consumers expect stable page tokens and HTTP error codes while newer streaming consumers expect partial/continuous events (for streaming embeddings and progressive rerank scoring). This ticket defines the product contract, acceptance criteria, and rollout approach for a checkpointed stream-to-page adapter that preserves error semantics and cursor parity across clients.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy paged clients can use page tokens produced by our adapter and see identical item ordering and stable next_page tokens for repeated queries (idempotent behavior).
Streaming clients receive partial events with explicit checkpoint tokens every N results; checkpoints can be exchanged for a page token to resume non-streaming iteration.

HTTP error code mappings are deterministic: map internal transient failures to 502/503 with retry-After hints, quota throttles to 429 with structured retry hints, and client validation errors to 400 series per existing contract. No legacy client receives new 2xx/3xx conditions than before.
End-to-end latency overhead introduced by adapter must be <5% p50 for standard embed/rerank calls in the baseline workload.
Comprehensive test suite validating cursor parity, idempotency, and error mapping with both streaming and paged client simulators included in CI.
technical_decisions: Adapter will emit structured streaming events: {type: 'partial', items: [...], checkpoint: 'cp_TOK'} and final events {type: 'final', checkpoint: 'cp_TOK_FINAL'}. Checkpoints are stable, opaque tokens signed with HMAC and contain a compact sequence and checksum.
Page tokens are a deterministic transformation of the latest checkpoint; decoder maintains backward-compatible token format for at least 12 months.

Error mapping table: internal transient rpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED -> 503 with retry_after seconds; rate limit -> 429 with 'retry_hint_ms'; validation failures -> 400 and include 'field' hint. Implement central mapper in proxy layer to avoid duplicating logic in runtime.
Idempotency: requests with idempotency-key header will be deduplicated at the gateway layer for 60s to preserve cursor stability across retries.
tradeoffs: Checkpoint frequency vs latency/throughput: more frequent checkpoints ease resumption but add metadata overhead; chosen default = every 64 items with opt param for callers.

HMAC-signed tokens vs server-side state: signed tokens allow stateless resumption across fleet but increase risks if token format needs to change; we add version prefix to tokens to allow graceful format migration.
Mapping errors conservatively favors backward compatibility (avoid surfacing new 2xx states) even if some modern clients could benefit from richer gRPC-style status.
implementation_notes: ENG spike completed (ENG-823401) validated checkpoint HMAC approach; prototype in go/proxy/stream-adapter branch. See PR #1456.
Runtime changes limited to adapter and proxy: no model runtime kernel changes required. This isolates risk for Dedicated/Private deployments.
Config flags: feature.toggle.embed_rerank_checkpointing (default: on for hosted, opt-in for dedicated/private until 2026-04).
Telemetry: emit 'compat.adapter.checkpoint_emitted' and 'compat.adapter.token_decoded' metrics; add slowpath tracing when token decode fails.
qa_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint encode/decode and token versioning matrix.
Integration test: streaming client consumes partial events -> exchanges latest checkpoint for page token -> continues via paged API; assertions on ordering and dedup.
Chaos test: inject transient rpc failures and assert deterministic HTTP mapping and idempotent resume semantics.
Performance smoke: run 1k QPS embed/rerank synthetic workload and record p50/p95 before and after adapter insertion.
rollout_plan: Canary deploy adapter to 5% of hosted traffic with feature flag and strict circuit breaker to bypass adapter on >2% error increase.
Collect 72-hour safety signals (errors, latency, customer-facing regressions) before 25% ramp.
Coordinate Dedicated/Private release notes and support playbook; use opt-in toggle and documented migration steps.
Deprecation policy: maintain legacy page-only tokens for 12 months after GA; publish migration guide and conversion tool.
